public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1067

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1067](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1067)
- [BoPi24] N. Bowler and M. Pitz, A note on uncountably chromatic graphs. arXiv:2402.05984 (2024).
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems. Acta Math. Acad.
  Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [Ko13] Komjáth, Péter, A note on chromatic number and connectivity of infinite graphs. Israel
  J. Math. (2013), 499--506.
- [So15] Soukup, Dániel T., Trees, ladders and graphs. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 96--116.
- [Th17] Thomassen, Carsten, Infinitely connected subgraphs in graphs of uncountable chromatic
  number. Combinatorica (2017), 785--793.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1067

/--
A graph is infinitely edge-connected if to disconnect the graph requires deleting
infinitely many edges. In other words, removing any finite set of edges leaves
the graph connected.
-/
def InfinitelyEdgeConnected {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃s : Set (Sym2 V)⦄, s.Finite → (G.deleteEdges s).Connected

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely connected subgraph with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$?

Komjáth [Ko13] proved that it is consistent that the answer is no. This was improved by
Soukup [So15], who constructed a counterexample using no extra set-theoretical assumptions. A
simpler elementary example was given by Bowler and Pitz [BoPi24].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and Aleph Prover.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1067.lean"]
theorem erdos_1067 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyConnected H.coe := by
  sorry

/--
Thomassen [Th17] constructed a counterexample to the version which asks for infinite
edge-connectivity (that is, to disconnect the graph requires deleting infinitely many edges).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1067.variants.infinite_edge_connectivity :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧ InfinitelyEdgeConnected H.coe := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Formalize variant independent of ZFC.

end Erdos1067

findings.description: The fixed `answer(False)` reverses the positive theorem proved in the cited [Th17]. The right-hand side asserts that every graph of chromatic cardinal ℵ₁ has an infinitely edge-connected subgraph of chromatic cardinal ℵ₁. Thomassen proves this: his subgraph has uncountable chromatic number, and its chromatic cardinal is at most that of the ambient graph, hence is exactly ℵ₁ here. Consequently, `False ↔` this universal assertion is false. The docstring's claim that Thomassen constructed a counterexample repeats the same polarity error. This is a reversal of the cited theorem, not a stale `research solved` category.
findings.source_evidence: Thomassen, “Infinitely connected subgraphs in graphs of uncountable chromatic number,” Theorem 2 (accepted manuscript, p. 5): “If G is a graph of uncountable chromatic number, then G has a subgraph which has infinite edge-connectivity and uncountable chromatic number.” The introduction explicitly says that “the edge-connectivity version of the conjecture is true.” https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/124108162/Erdos_Hajnal_final.pdf ; also the publisher abstract at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00493-016-3436-4 .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `answer(False)` with `answer(True)`, leaving the right-hand side unchanged. Replace the counterexample docstring with a statement that Thomassen proved the infinite edge-connectivity version. Keep `category research solved`.

reformulations.difference: The later Erdős–Hajnal question quoted in Soukup's introduction requests an uncountably chromatic subgraph; Lean requests chromatic cardinal exactly ℵ₁.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the ambient hypothesis χ(G)=ℵ₁, restricting a coloring gives χ(H)≤χ(G)=ℵ₁ for every subgraph H. Since ℵ₁ is the least uncountable cardinal, χ(H)>ℵ₀ is equivalent to χ(H)=ℵ₁. Both the pointwise equivalence and the equivalence of the full universal questions were proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without using either admitted problem theorem.

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over all finite sets of unordered vertex pairs, rather than only finite subsets of the graph's actual edge set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting a pair that is not an edge has no effect: `G.deleteEdges s = G.deleteEdges (s ∩ G.edgeSet)`. The intersection is finite whenever s is finite. Thus the definition is equivalent to quantifying only over finite actual edge sets. This equivalence was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`.

sources_consulted: Bowler and Pitz, A note on uncountably chromatic graphs, arXiv:2402.05984v2: abstract/version history at https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05984 and full LaTeX source from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2402.05984 .

Soukup, Trees, ladders and graphs, arXiv:1409.2922, published J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 115 (2015), 96–116: LaTeX source from https://arxiv.org/e-print/1409.2922 ; introduction, connectivity definitions, main counterexample theorem, and remarks.

Erdős and Hajnal, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems (1966), especially pp. 61 and 77: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1966-07.pdf ; bibliographic and publisher records at https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html and https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02020444 .
Komjáth, A note on chromatic number and connectivity of infinite graphs (2013), publisher abstract and references: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11856-012-0176-z .

Thomassen, Infinitely connected subgraphs in graphs of uncountable chromatic number: accepted manuscript, especially §§1–2 and Theorem 2, https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/portalfiles/portal/124108162/Erdos_Hajnal_final.pdf ; publisher abstract https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00493-016-3436-4 ; author-repository record https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/2a40e941-8bd7-4f9b-a41c-48dc0495fc2e .
Cited external Lean proof, including its definitions and final `not_erdos_1067` theorem: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1067.lean .

Crossref bibliographic records for the Thomassen and Komjáth papers; OpenAlex DOI records https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-016-3436-4 and https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1007/s11856-012-0176-z ; Semantic Scholar DOI record for the Thomassen paper (used to locate full text).
review.notes: Checked all three mathematical declarations and the imported definitions. The main theorem faithfully addresses the unrestricted-size question discussed by Soukup; the original size-ℵ₁ variant is a distinct, independent problem, as the TODO recognizes. Lean sanity checks establish that chromaticCardinal is an attained minimum, that the ℵ₁ hypothesis is satisfiable, and that empty/countable graphs cannot satisfy it. The Erdős webpage remained behind a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so comparison used the cited primary literature directly. The linked external proof was inspected and contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Its original Lean/mathlib 4.24.0 project was not available for kernel replay; attempting it with the supplied 4.33.1 environment produced API incompatibilities, from which no status defect is inferred.

not_demonstrated.reason: Refuting the exact statement `False ↔ ∀ V G, …` requires proving its entire universal right-hand side: Thomassen’s positive edge-connectivity theorem. A single graph cannot refute this negated universal, and finite graphs cannot satisfy the chromatic-cardinal ℵ₁ hypothesis. No proved library result supplying the required theorem was found; proving it would require substantial mathematics.

submission.summary: The polarity mismatch is supported by the cited source, but it does not admit a short, honest Lean demonstration. No trivial_proof.lean file was created.
submission.gave_up_reason: The only reported defect requires a nontrivial universal theorem to disprove the formalized statement. Assuming that theorem or relying on admitted problem declarations would not provide the requested honest demonstration.

submission.summary: Changed the edge-connectivity variant from answer(False) to answer(True) and corrected its docstring to say Thomassen proved this version. Left the right-hand side, attributes, and all other declarations unchanged. The specified compile command succeeds with only the expected `sorry` warnings.
